title: 2025 Red Snapper Private Angling Component Closure in Gulf Federal Waters Off Texas
summary:
NOAA Fisheries will close red snapper fishing for private anglers in federal waters off Texas from November 21, 2025, until January 1, 2026. The goal is to keep Texas within its annual catch limit and help prevent overfishing, while allowing the state to keep its own season open in state waters.

This move mainly benefits the long-term health of the red snapper population and anglers who value stable, predictable access in future years. It also supports Texas’s approach to managing its share of the catch by shifting late-season fishing to state waters, where the state can better track and control harvest.

Those most likely to feel the pinch are private anglers who prefer fishing deeper, federal waters late in the year, as well as coastal businesses that rely on those private trips during the holiday period. There may also be some confusion for visitors, since the closure applies to all private anglers in federal waters off Texas regardless of where they live or where they plan to land their catch. By contrast, federally permitted charter and headboat operations are managed under a different system, so this specific closure does not apply to them.

The closure stems from a state request under an existing federal-state management framework. Texas already asked for, and received, a federal-water closure at the start of 2025, and this second closure helps ensure the state stays within its yearly limit. During the closure, private anglers may not harvest or possess red snapper in federal waters off Texas, and the bag limit there is zero. State waters remain open year-round under Texas rules.
